title: Fynaptix · AI & Compute Research
heading: AI & Compute Intelligence
subheading: The capex supercycle, silicon stack, foundation-model giants & the bubble debate
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. AI is the market's most crowded trade; concentration and drawdown risk are significant. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Amazon (~$220B), Alphabet ($195–205B), Microsoft (capex guide raised to ~$190B CY2026 from ~$175B / ~$255–260B FY2027 all-in), Meta ($130–145B after twice raising its floor) and Oracle (S&P models $90–95B FY2027 capex, distinct from Oracle's own $90B+ revenue guide) — combined $825–855B. Debt funding still sits near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet); Wall Street estimates ~$300B of AI-linked investment-grade debt issuance for 2026, which BofA says has added ~0.3 percentage points to 10-year Treasury yields, with hyperscaler borrowing alone equal to roughly 25% of net Treasury note/bond issuance to private investors (Nomura)

kpis.sub: ANTHROPIC'S IPO TARGET VS. OPENAI'S LATEST PRIVATE MARK
kpis.label: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to anchor-invest up to $10B in Anthropic's IPO, which could raise as much as $100B and value the company at roughly $2.0–2.3 trillion — pricing is targeted before the November 2026 U.S. midterms; revenue run-rate topped $65B annualized at end of July, with investors modeling $190–200B by 2028. OpenAI remains marked at $852B (set via its ~$122B primary round/August employee tender), crossed $40B in annualized revenue in August, but filed only a confidential S-1 and isn't expected to list until 2027

Global venture funding per Crunchbase ($300B in Q1, $205B in Q2), already topping all of 2025's $440B; AI captured ~70–80% of it. US-only venture deployment reached $412.7B in H1 2026, of which 86% went to AI companies (PitchBook). OpenAI and Anthropic alone absorbed $217B — 43% of every venture dollar invested worldwide this year; Mistral reportedly landed a fresh ~$3.5B round this week, details still emerging, another sign the mega-round pace hasn't slowed

kpis.sub: TSMC's AUGUST REVENUE GROWTH — NOW WARNING NVIDIA & BROADCOM OF A CAPACITY SQUEEZE
kpis.label: TSMC's August monthly revenue accelerated to +53% YoY (from +44.7% in July) as HPC/AI demand keeps outrunning supply; the company has reportedly warned Nvidia and Broadcom of a capacity squeeze even as it raises its 2026 revenue growth outlook to "slightly above 40%" and lifts 2026 capex to $60–64B — an unusual case of a supplier telling its two biggest customers it can't keep up

bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The industry has now committed an estimated $3–4T to AI infrastructure against an annualized return requirement of roughly $600–800B in new profit (up from Sequoia's original $200B framework in late 2023), while actual AI-attributable revenue runs an estimated $50–150B a year — a gap that keeps widening as the top-5 hyperscaler 2026/FY27 capex total climbs to $825–855B. For context, cloud computing's capex-to-revenue ratio at the same point in its adoption curve (2011) was roughly 2.4:1, far below today's multiple. The BIS's June 2026 annual report still names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: Rates are the transmission mechanism — but strength can still win the argument
bear_case.description: The 30-year Treasury eased slightly to ~5.36% on Sept 11 after touching its highest level since 2007 — still elevated as AI-linked debt issuance adds to bond-supply pressure. BofA estimates the surge in AI-related corporate debt sales has added roughly 0.3 percentage points to 10-year rates this year, and Nomura pegs hyperscaler borrowing alone at ~25% of net Treasury note/bond issuance to private investors. But Oracle's Sept 10 beat-and-raise, which sent the stock up ~15% on the week, kept the fundamental-demand side of the argument intact — a reminder the debate can swing hard in either direction week to week.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments sitting off hyperscaler balance sheets, with debt funding of the buildout holding near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet). Oracle remains the starkest case on the balance sheet — still BBB- (one notch above junk) with FY26 free cash flow at -$23.7B and S&P still modeling a ~$42B FY27 deficit — even though this week's Q1 FY2027 results (revenue +30%, Cloud Infrastructure +121%) were genuinely strong, and Larry Ellison canceling a planned $7.5B stock sale reads as a bullish insider signal. The credit risk and the operating momentum are both real; they haven't yet reconciled.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to anchor-invest up to $10B in Anthropic's own IPO — a chipmaker taking a stake in the public offering of one of its largest customers — on top of the existing $105B OpenAI Ohio data-center financing guarantee. Michael Burry has escalated, calling Nvidia's revenue "majority circularly financed" and adding shorts on Oracle, Micron and Nebius plus March 2027 puts on the semiconductor ETF. Analysts have tallied more than $800B in criss-crossing investment and purchase commitments across the broader AI supply chain, a pattern CNBC's Jim Cramer publicly compared to dot-com-era financing. Nvidia's Sept 10 "Sovereign Intelligence" tie-up with Palantir extends the web further still, deepening ties between the chip layer and the application layer.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years; bears argue the real economic life is closer to 2–3 years, understating depreciation by an estimated ~$176B across 2026–2028 and flattering reported earnings (Oracle by an estimated 26.9%, Meta by 20.8%, by 2028 on this analysis). Michael Burry has doubled down on shorts in Oracle, Micron and Nebius, plus fresh March 2027 puts on the semiconductor ETF, calling current pricing "what the top of a boom looks like." Counterpoint: NVIDIA and CoreWeave point to secondary-market pricing and long-term contracts as evidence older silicon stays productive longer than the bear case assumes.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Tech-sector layoffs have now crossed 128,536 workers across 299 companies in 2026 through Sept 10 (Layoffs.fyi) — already exceeding all of 2025 — with more than 6,300 cuts in the first ten days of September alone, led by Uber's ~3,300-role reduction. Meta itself reassigned ~7,000 staff into Applied AI this month after cutting ~8,000 (10% of the workforce) in May, and is now reconsidering its own flatter-org structure. The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, record layoffs, and organizational whiplash even at companies with strong core businesses — keeps fueling the argument that AI economics lean partly on cost-cutting elsewhere, not purely on AI revenue.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took 43% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total, and AI took 86% of all US venture dollars in H1 per PitchBook), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once. NVIDIA now sits at the center of deals spanning chips (TSMC, Broadcom), model hosting (Hugging Face), enterprise software (Palantir) and now a potential anchor stake in Anthropic's IPO — a single company's balance sheet increasingly touches nearly every layer of this page. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters and Oracle's Sept 10 beat is a live example — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals.
